problem: The trap says the DC-bus capacitors are counted per leg ('two capacitors and two clamping diodes per leg'), and that the counts are 'not per whole inverter'. Only the clamping diodes are per leg. The m−1 DC-bus capacitors form the shared DC bus for the whole inverter, not one set per leg; a three-phase three-level NPC has two DC-bus capacitors in total, not two per leg.
fix: NPC has m−1 DC-bus capacitors for the whole inverter (shared by all legs) and (m−1)(m−2) clamping diodes per leg. For three-level: two DC-bus capacitors in total and two clamping diodes per leg.

problem: 'A diode-clamped leg, also called neutral-point-clamped (NPC)' treats the two names as fully interchangeable. NPC is really the three-level diode-clamped circuit; four- and five-level diode-clamped legs are usually just called diode-clamped.
fix: Say: 'A diode-clamped leg (the three-level version is called neutral-point-clamped, NPC) uses one DC bus split by m−1 capacitors.'
